# the contributor audit: three homothetic fibers and the global star obstruction



## Three positive homothetic fibers

I read the complete proof in `candidate aae24573a37976a6` and its subset-tail dependency, Sections 6–7 of `candidate dafd411c026c302c`. I reran `supporting computation verify_three_homothetic_all_ratios.py`: PASS for 3534 exact scalar checks, 721 radius cases, 6400 actual triangular caps, and the vertical caps.

The allowed affine shear centers the middle and larger endpoint, with Jacobian one on every continuous fiber. The residual translation satisfies the stated support-function containment. The nested case, heavy-fiber cases, and strictly nonheavy strip exhaust all radius triples. In the strip the positive-radius translated trimmed copy is contained both in the actual small endpoint and in the centered larger endpoint. Its cap payment and the additional middle cap are at exactly the same point and normal; no fiber or cap mass is charged twice.

The scalar inequality is correct: the worst scale ratio is one, the unique minimum of the convex scalar expression is correctly computed, and Jensen bounds it by two with equality in dimension two. The stronger coefficient one half implies the required Gamma coefficient. Closed nonvertical cut boundaries are volume-null; vertical through-point caps contain the whole middle and an endpoint. All chosen points belong to original fibers. The dimension-one result is a separate proved interval theorem, not an application of the invalid dimension-one trimming inequality.

The arbitrary-middle, comparable-homothetic-endpoint theorem also passes: the endpoint midpoint body supplies the same actual point as the paired copies, the golden-ratio volume condition gives the stated payment, and the actual middle centroid is used only in its heavy case.

## Unequal pair interpolation and displacement

The previously read unequal-pair interpolation and centroid-defect notes have no new mathematical gap. This turn I reran `supporting computation verify_unequal_pair_source_interpolation.py` (629 exact checks) and `supporting computation verify_homothetic_pair_centroid_defect.py` (80 exact offset cases), both PASS. In particular the displacement gauge is nonsymmetric, and its orientation is retained. The sharp dimension coefficient is not replaced by one.

## Global failure of the maximal reflected-pair gauge certificate

I read all seven sections of `candidate 0c151a0c56ccc06f` and reran its exact verifier: PASS for all 18 central candidates and 170 noncentral envelopes, all mass constants, and the independent OC-safety comparison. The independent degeneracy audit checks the referenced sampling theorem in detail.

Permutation averaging decreases every displacement gauge. The own simplex cap bound on the resulting vertex axis is exact. Negative axis displacement is dominated by the own centroid, simultaneously for every reflected pair. On each interval between successive pair centroids the central objective is convex, including at a zero of a positive-part term, so its maximum is attained in the displayed finite table.

For a noncentral anchor k>=0 the pair midpoint and radius depend on max(k,h). The proved lower-bound function Phi, not the actual minimum cap cost, is at most 2 Gamma times the midpoint radius to the dth power. This distinction is essential: the corresponding actual-cap lower claim was already disproved. After this upper comparison, every noncentral pair is dominated by the central pair with the same index h, and the own term is identical on the common axis. Extra central terms are nonnegative. Base reflection handles negative k. Thus the same strict shortfall holds globally for this particular certificate over every original candidate point, with no claim that the actual depth has that shortfall.

## Nonproduct reflection

I read the complete affine-radius realization and its independent explicit base-depth certificate, and reran both verifiers. PASS. The pentagon includes the inequality u>=-1, all twelve bases are present, and the radius is positive and affine throughout the real polygon. The exact reflection maximum is below one quarter of total weight. At the explicit base (0,1), the separate weighted halfspace bound exceeds one quarter and transfers by ordinary Grünbaum to every actual ambient cap for any common centered shape. This is another failure of a proposed sufficient invariant, not an OC counterexample.
